steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the key differences at a glance:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA: deoxyribose (no 2′-OH group)  
   • RNA: ribose (has 2′-OH group)  

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), guanine (G)  
   • RNA: adenine (A), uracil (U) replaces thymine, cytosine (C), guanine (G)  

3. Strandedness & structure  
   • DNA: usually a double helix—two complementary strands for stability and long-term storage  
   • RNA: usually single-stranded—can fold into complex 3D shapes  

4. Function  
   • DNA: permanent repository of genetic information (in the nucleus of eukaryotes)  
   • RNA: transient messenger (mRNA), adaptor (tRNA), structural/catalytic (rRNA, ribozymes) in gene expression  

5. Stability  
   • DNA: chemically more stable—ideal for long-term storage  
   • RNA: less stable (the 2′-OH makes it more reactive)—suited to dynamic roles in the cell.
